PRIMARY CITATION IS DOUBLE-EDGED / MIS-DEPLOYED: The verbatim understanding quote ('In cases where the link takes one to a document or a web application, the name of the document or web application would be sufficient to describe the purpose of the link...') actually argues FOR a pass here. The link's href ends in /recipes/kabsa.pdf (a document) and its accessible name 'كبسة الدجاج بالخطوات' is essentially the title of that very PDF document (the kabsa recipe). By the literal text of the quote, naming the link with the document's name is sufficient. The .md's parenthetical claim that the name is 'the ARTICLE's title, not the document the link downloads' is strained — the PDF is the article rendered as a document and shares the same title. The quote that best supports the FAILURE is the G91 one ('distinguish this link from links... that lead to other destinations'), not the cited understanding sentence.

FAILURE RATIONALE SHIFTS UNDER SCRUTINY: The genuinely defensible 'failed' verdict rests on (a) no indication the control is a DOWNLOAD vs. a navigation/anchor, and (b) the identical name appearing as both the h1 (AX backendNodeId 19, heading L1) and the link (backendNodeId 21) creating in-context ambiguity. The .md leads instead with 'names the article not the action', which the cited understanding sentence partly rebuts. The outcome label is still correct, but the documented mechanism leans on the weaker of the two citations.

SEVERE PROMPT/FILE MISMATCH: The task prompt describes a completely different page than the one on disk. Prompt claims a 'charity grant-spending page' with THREE 'Download this data' links (PDF/XLSX/CSV) of one equivalent dataset, expected outcome PASSED, selector 'p > a[download$=".pdf"], p > a[download$=".xlsx"], p > a[download$=".csv"]'. The ACTUAL file (case-02.html) is a swim-school page with TWO '.txt' links named 'download the form' inside a single <td>, resolving to GENUINELY DIFFERENT documents (parental-consent vs medical-history), expected outcome FAILED. grep confirms '.pdf/.xlsx/.csv/Download this data' appear 0 times in the file; the prompt selector matches nothing. The prompt's 'Claimed expected outcome: passed' is wrong for this file.

The file itself is internally consistent and correct: HTML, MD, AX tree, and citation all agree it is a 2.4.4 FAIL (two identical-name links in the same cell -> non-equivalent resources, disambiguation only in prose not in name/programmatic context).

All citations verified verbatim: MD's Description quote matches fd3a94.md line 21 char-for-char; the prompt's Expectation quote matches fd3a94.md lines 43-47 char-for-char; the Understanding 'same sentence/paragraph/list item/table cell' quote is accurate. No citation defect on the file.

DOC-PRECISION (minor, not an outcome error): The doc asserts this 'matches fd3a94 Failed Example 4' and is a 'same context' failure, but the two structures are NOT structurally equivalent. In fd3a94 Failed Example 4 both <a> elements share ONE container span (literally 'the same' programmatically determined context), satisfying the ACT rule's applicability. In case-04 the two links live in SEPARATE <div class='buyrow col1'> / '...col2' cells (AX tree confirms distinct parent generics backendNodeId 33 vs 35). Under fd3a94's OWN taxonomy this is the Inapplicable-Example-6 pattern ('different programmatically determined link contexts because the div elements place them in different display blocks'), which would make the ACT rule fd3a94 arguably INAPPLICABLE, not failed.

The page still genuinely FAILS WCAG 2.4.4 via the broader F63 path (each link's own bare cell carries no plan/price; destinations differ $9 vs $99; disambiguation is visual-only). fd3a94 Background (line 53) explicitly concedes such identical-but-separate-context cases 'also fail 2.4.4' but were left out of the ACT rule as infeasible to automate. So 'failed' is correct, but the citation framing slightly over-claims the fd3a94 Example-4 fit; it should be framed primarily as F63 / general 2.4.4.
Both cited quotes verified VERBATIM: fd3a94.md line 484 (Failed Example 4) and F63.html line 10 match character-for-character.
